reason: The text recounts Jacob and Rebekah's successful deception of the patriarch Isaac. Rather than portraying regular people as wrongly challenging rightful leadership, the narrative shows Jacob (a younger, lower-status person) and his mother orchestrating an elaborate fraud against the family patriarch. Jacob deceives his elderly father and wrongfully obtains the blessing intended for his older brother Esau. Isaac is portrayed as the victim of deception, not as a rightfully vindicated authority figure. The story emphasizes the cunning by which a person of lower status circumvents the established order and succeeds through duplicity—the opposite of a narrative validating leadership authority and condemning popular challenge to it.
